First textbook Mercury flight — 6 orbits; double Glenn / Carpenter duration

After two flights that ended in scares, Sigma 7 was the one that was boring on purpose — and that was the achievement. Wally Schirra called it a textbook engineering test and flew it like one: minimal experiments, careful conservation of every kilogram of fuel and every amp of power, six orbits spent proving the spacecraft could be operated with discipline rather than wrestled. He splashed down almost on top of the recovery carrier. In a program that had been improvising under pressure, Sigma 7 showed the Americans had learned to fly the thing calmly — the prerequisite for the far longer missions ahead.

Wally Schirra's 6-orbit flight — doubled Glenn's and Carpenter's mission length. Schirra called his flight a "textbook engineering test" — minimal experimental load, focus on conserving consumables, validating the vehicle for longer duration. Flight duration 9 h 13 min; orbital parameters 161 × 283 km. Splashed down ~445 km NE of Midway in the Pacific — first Mercury flight to splash in the Pacific. Schirra used so little attitude-control fuel that he dumped the rest during re-entry. Capsule Sigma 7 on display at the Heroes and Legends hall of the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, FL.
Atlas LV-3B from Cape Canaveral LC-14 1962-10-03 12:15 UTC.
Pacific Ocean ~445 km NE of Midway after 6 orbits / 9 h 13 min. First Mercury Pacific recovery.
